purpose: Post-v0.1 spec close. RQ9 settles the form of K (fixed taxonomy vs inheritance lattice vs free constraint-bag). RQ10 settles whether the layer-seam is a primitive of A*, a new integrity constraint IC4, or derivable from IC3 + the 9 ops. RQ12 measures the net cost of two-layer separation: does c_modify rise more than c_drift falls?
context_summary: v0 frozen 2026-05-21. v0.1 reference impl shipped 2026-05-21 at /impl/a_star/ (40/40 tests). v0.1 two-layer consolidation shipped 2026-05-22: Layer A /Core/Neural/neural-gtm/ (engine, tenant-agnostic) + Layer B /Core/Neural/Buuuk/ (tenant). A* primitives dropped 111 -> 71 across the split (~36%). Engineering agent gained Layer A/B awareness; cross-layer changesets trip a `block` severity gate. QA agent (MBT engine) gained two new FSM scopes (layer_a_engine, layer_b_tenant) and two seam invariants: tenant_cannot_mutate_engine_state, engine_cannot_read_tenant_secrets. The engine repo neural-gtm does NOT cleanly fit any of the 7 v0 K classes (closest is product-saas but neural-gtm has no end-users). This triggers RQ9. The seam invariants are currently enforced only in QA, not declared in A_STAR_v0.md, which triggers RQ10. The 36% primitive drop is partial evidence for the seam being net-positive but does not isolate c_modify vs c_drift contributions, which triggers RQ12.

threads.title: What is the right form for K in A*(I, L, K, T)? Fixed taxonomy, inheritance lattice, or free constraint-bag?
threads.input:
In A*(I, L, K, T) -> (A, D), K is the constraint profile. v0 defines K as a fixed taxonomy of 7 named classes: outbound-pipeline, content-pipeline, product-marketing, product-saas, research-memory, audit-pipeline, intel-pipeline. Each class is a tuple (H_K, W_K, T_K, F_K, E_K) where H_K is hard constraints, W_K is C_core weights, T_K is required tools, F_K is required fields, E_K is excluded patterns.

The trigger: the engine repo /Core/Neural/neural-gtm/ does not fit any of the 7 classes. It is a tenant-agnostic substrate that ships pipelines, not a pipeline itself. Its closest match is product-saas (the TUHH seed) but it has no end-users, no auth, no billing. Forcing K=outbound-pipeline (what we did for the solver run) gives a SAT result but wrong-K-class semantics: the engine has no leads, no SMTP, no cohorts.

Three candidate forms for K:

(1) Fixed taxonomy. Add an 8th class engine-of-K, then a 9th when the next meta-pattern appears. Simple, but every meta-pattern needs a new class.

(2) Inheritance lattice. K-classes derive from each other via formal operators. engine-of(outbound-pipeline) is derived from outbound-pipeline by lifting tenant-specific constraints into tenant-agnostic ones. The 7 stay frozen as bootstrap. Derivation rules are mechanical.

(3) Free constraint-bag. K dissolves as a named entity. Each folder declares its own (H, W, T, F, E) directly in its .manifest.yaml. Predicates compose. Loses the K-as-prior advantage (e.g. weight defaults from H_K); gains maximum expressiveness.

Research tasks:

1. Survey the literature on taxonomy form in software architecture and adjacent fields. Cover: (a) Reynolds and Aitchison on biological taxonomy vs phylogenetic trees (closed-set classification vs evolutionary derivation), (b) library science classification systems (Dewey vs UDC vs LCSH; Ranganathan's faceted classification), (c) ontology engineering on closed-set vs derived classes (OWL subclass hierarchies, RDFS), (d) type theory on nominal vs structural typing (Java nominal, TypeScript structural, Haskell typeclass), (e) constraint logic programming on constraint sets vs constraint profiles. For each, summarize what worked and what failed when the domain grew.

2. Survey the literature on architecture-pattern catalogs and how they handled growth. Cover: GoF design patterns (closed 23 patterns, criticized for not growing), POSA series (Buschmann et al, growable but not derivable), DDD bounded contexts (free-form per project), microservice patterns (Richardson's catalog, semi-closed), data mesh quanta (Dehghani, derived from domain). Discuss which model scales and which atrophies as new patterns appear.

3. Survey the constraint-modeling literature on profile vs lattice vs bag forms. Cover: (a) MiniZinc and OR-Tools constraint profiles (CP solvers' notion of model families), (b) feature-modeling in software product lines (FODA, feature diagrams, lattice of valid configurations), (c) configuration-management on constraint inheritance (Puppet/Chef/Ansible role hierarchies), (d) policy-as-code on rule inheritance (OPA/Rego, Cedar), (e) type-class hierarchies in Haskell/Scala (lattice-shaped constraint inheritance). Identify which form best supports both (a) bootstrap learning from a small fixed set and (b) graceful extension to novel cases.

4. Define the formal lattice operators if K is a lattice. Candidates: lift_tenant (turn tenant-specific constraints into tenant-agnostic ones; produces the engine-of-X family), restrict_scope (narrow a class to a subdomain; e.g., outbound-pipeline restricted to B2B-only or to SMTP-only), compose(K1, K2) (combine two profiles into a hybrid; e.g., content-pipeline composed with audit-pipeline yields content-with-provenance), specialize_tenant (the inverse of lift_tenant). For each operator, specify input form, output form, soundness condition (operator preserves the well-formedness of (H, W, T, F, E)), and a worked example.

5. For the free-bag form, address how the simplicity prior is recovered. v0 inherits a simplicity prior from S(M,T) (the H_simp regularizer per RQ8). In the fixed-taxonomy form, H_simp is encoded in W_K defaults. In the lattice form, H_simp is inherited along the derivation chain. In the free-bag form, the prior must be declared per-folder, which risks every folder reinventing it. Propose a mechanism (per-class library, schema default, learned-from-corpus prior).

6. Empirical pass: the 8 Neural projects (Buuuk, MAIKAI, TUHH, Personal Twin, SI Engine, si-global-intel, Longevity-Science-Daily, Healome). For each, list the K declarations that would be needed under each of the three forms. Identify which projects cleanly fit one v0 class, which span multiple, which need a new class, and which exemplify a meta-pattern (engine, harness, lab). The empirical evidence should bias the recommendation.

7. Discuss how each form changes the COP encoding in /impl/a_star/solver/model.py. (a) Fixed: build_model takes k_class as a string, looks up W_K from the registry. (b) Lattice: build_model takes k_class as a derivation expression, materializes (H, W, T, F, E) by traversing the lattice. (c) Free: build_model reads (H, W, T, F, E) directly from the folder's manifest. Sketch the API change for each and estimate the impact on the Z3 model size and the soft-objective shape.

8. Address the lifecycle question: K can evolve over a project's lifetime (an outbound-pipeline that adds a UI becomes outbound-pipeline-with-saas). Which form handles K evolution most cleanly? Fixed (re-classify), lattice (re-derive), or free (mutate the bag)?

9. Make a recommendation: which of the three forms should v0.2 of A* adopt? Reason from (a) the survey evidence on what scaled in adjacent fields, (b) the empirical fit on 8 Neural projects, (c) the COP encoding impact, (d) the lifecycle handling. State the recommendation as a precise formal definition replacing the v0 definition 'K is one of 7 classes'.

10. Identify the falsifiers. Under the recommended form, what observation would force a revision? Example for lattice: a project that fits no derivation chain from the 7 bootstrap classes; or a derivation that requires an operator outside the four (lift_tenant, restrict_scope, compose, specialize_tenant). Be specific.

Deliverable: a structured research memo with the literature survey, the formal lattice-operator definitions if lattice is preferred, the per-project empirical fit table for all 8 Neural projects, the COP encoding sketches, the recommendation with reasoning, and the falsifier list. Full citations.

threads.title: Is the layer seam (engine vs tenant) a primitive of A*, a new integrity constraint, or derivable from existing primitives?
threads.input:
A* v0 defines three integrity constraints (IC1 canonicality, IC2 declared retention + verifiable disposition, IC3 manifest consistency = folder-as-contract) and 9 primitive operations (CREATE_FOLDER, ARCHIVE_FOLDER, MOVE_ARTIFACT, DUPLICATE_TO_CACHE, SET_SOURCE_OF_TRUTH, UPDATE_MANIFEST, UPSERT_RELATION, MIGRATE_PERSISTENCE, SCHEDULE_DESTRUCTION).

The trigger: v0.1 consolidation introduced a two-layer architecture: Layer A engine (/Core/Neural/neural-gtm/, tenant-agnostic, reusable) and Layer B tenant (/Core/Neural/Buuuk/, tenant-specific). The QA agent now enforces two seam invariants: (a) tenant_cannot_mutate_engine_state (a transition originating in Layer B that writes to a Layer A path is a violation), (b) engine_cannot_read_tenant_secrets (a transition originating in Layer A that reads a tenant secret pattern .env / secrets/ / credentials/ is a violation).

Three candidate placements for these invariants:

(a) New primitive operation(s). Add DECLARE_LAYER and BIND_SEAM to the 9-op set. The solver explicitly emits them; downstream tools enforce.

(b) New integrity constraint IC4. 'Every folder has a declared layer label in {engine, tenant_X, shared}, and inter-layer access satisfies the seam invariants.' Joins IC1/IC2/IC3 as a top-level invariant.

(c) Derivable. The seam invariants are corollaries of IC3 (folder-as-contract). A folder's manifest declares its layer; cross-layer access becomes a manifest contract violation; the existing 9 ops are sufficient to declare and enforce the seam. No spec change needed beyond a worked example.

Research tasks:

1. Survey the software-architecture literature on layer separation and how layering is formally specified. Cover: (a) Parnas's information hiding and the 'uses' relation, (b) Bass/Clements/Kazman on architectural views and layered styles, (c) hexagonal architecture / ports and adapters (Cockburn), (d) onion architecture (Palermo), (e) clean architecture (Martin), (f) the dependency rule and how it is checked (ArchUnit, Structurizr, NDepend), (g) the difference between a 'soft' layer (convention) and a 'hard' layer (compiler/loader enforces). For each, identify whether layer membership is declared per-component, derived from path/package, or asserted globally.

2. Survey the multi-tenant architecture literature. Cover: (a) Krebs/Momm/Kounev tenant isolation taxonomy, (b) the SaaS multi-tenancy patterns (shared everything, shared database/separate schema, separate database), (c) cloud-platform isolation models (Kubernetes namespaces, AWS Organizations + SCP, GCP folder hierarchy), (d) the difference between 'tenant data isolation' (rows) and 'tenant code isolation' (which is what the engine/tenant seam is about). For each, identify whether the engine/tenant boundary is a property of the data model or a property of the codebase.

3. Survey the capability-security literature on read/write asymmetries across boundaries. Cover: (a) Lampson's protection matrix, (b) the Bell-LaPadula no-read-up/no-write-down rules, (c) the Biba integrity model (no-write-up/no-read-down), (d) information flow control (IFC) and noninterference (Goguen-Meseguer), (e) capability-based access (KeyKOS, EROS, seL4), (f) JavaScript SES and ocap (Miller, Stiegler). The seam invariants resemble Biba (no-write-up: tenant cannot mutate engine state) plus a confidentiality cut (no-read-down: engine cannot read tenant secrets). Map the seam invariants formally into one of these models and discuss soundness.

4. Survey the schema-evolution literature on co-evolution of a 'core' and 'extensions'. Cover: (a) WordPress core vs plugins, (b) Kubernetes CRD vs operator separation, (c) database engine vs extension (Postgres extensions), (d) browser engine vs extension. For each, identify the formal mechanism by which the core protects itself from the extension and vice versa. Is it a manifest, a typed interface, a runtime sandbox, or convention?

5. Address the formal question: under IC3 (folder-as-contract), what additional declaration is needed to recover the seam invariants? Specifically, if a folder's manifest declares a 'layer' field with values {engine, tenant_X, shared}, and IC3 already requires manifest consistency across folder boundaries, do the seam invariants follow as theorems? If yes, the seam is derivable (option c). If no, identify what additional axiom is needed and whether that axiom is best placed as (a) a new primitive op or (b) a new integrity constraint.

6. Evaluate the three placements against three criteria: (a) minimality (Occam's razor: fewer axioms wins), (b) spec stability (placement that requires fewest future spec edits as new layer patterns emerge), (c) implementation cost (impact on solver, validator, QA agent). Score each placement.

7. Address the generalization question: are there other 'seams' the same machinery should handle? Candidates: dev/prod seam, public/private seam, human-edited/machine-generated seam, secret/non-secret seam, billable/non-billable seam. For each, identify whether the recommended placement (from task 6) generalizes cleanly.

8. Specify how S(M, T) generalizes when layers are introduced. v0's S(M, T) is A* restricted to K=routing with fixed folder/naming/archival/persistence. Does S(M, T, L) with L=layer change the formal reduction proven in RQ8, or is L absorbed by K (a per-layer K profile)?

9. Make a recommendation: which placement should v0.2 adopt? State the recommendation as a precise textual diff against A_STAR_v0.md (which sentences change, which sections are added).

10. Identify the falsifiers. Under the recommended placement, what observation would force a revision? Be specific.

Deliverable: a structured research memo with the literature survey, the formal mapping into Bell-LaPadula or Biba, the IC3-derivation sketch, the three-placement scoring matrix, the generalization analysis, the recommendation with the precise A_STAR_v0.md diff, and the falsifier list. Full citations.

threads.title: What is the net cost of two-layer separation? Does c_modify rise more than c_drift falls?
threads.input:
v0.1 consolidation split a single ogilvy repo into two: Layer A engine /Core/Neural/neural-gtm/ (31 folders) + Layer B tenant /Core/Neural/Buuuk/ (55 folders). A* primitive count dropped from 111 (pre) to 71 (post-split sum), a ~36% reduction. The drop comes from IC3 (folder-as-contract) being more easily satisfied at smaller, semantically homogeneous roots. But primitive count is not the same as C_core total. The seam should:

- Lower c_drift (engine and tenant evolve on separate cadences; each can be reviewed independently).
- Raise c_modify (cross-cutting changes now touch two repos plus the seam shim).
- Likely lower c_loss (tenant blast radius confined; an engine bug does not corrupt tenant data).
- Possibly raise c_storage (engine + tenant duplicate some artifacts like venv, README, license).
- Effect on c_money and c_find unclear.

Decides whether two-layer separation is the default architecture for K=outbound-pipeline (and likely most K classes) or an optimization triggered only when c_drift exceeds a threshold.

Research tasks:

1. Survey the software-engineering literature on the cost of modularization. Cover: (a) Parnas 1972 on the criteria to be used in decomposing systems into modules (and its claim that the right decomposition reduces total cost despite localized increases), (b) the monorepo vs polyrepo debate (Bazel/Google, Meta/Mononoke, Microsoft Git, Improbable/Spotify case studies), (c) the microservices cost literature (Newman, Fowler 'microservices premium', the 'distributed monolith' antipattern), (d) Conway's Law and its inverse, (e) the modularity tax in build systems (incremental compile times, dependency-graph fan-out). Extract concrete numbers where available (e.g., 'Google internal monorepo reports X% build-time impact when project Y was split').

2. Survey the empirical literature on the cost of cross-cutting changes. Cover: (a) MacCormack/Baldwin/Rusnak on the architecture of complex systems (DSM analysis, propagation cost metrics), (b) the change-coupling literature (D'Ambros, Gall, Lanza on co-change), (c) the technical-debt literature on cross-component change cost (Tom et al, Kruchten). Identify metrics that approximate c_modify (number of files touched per change, breadth of test impact, build cone size).

3. Survey the empirical literature on drift in monorepos vs polyrepos. Cover: (a) shared-vs-versioned dependencies (the Google diamond-dependency problem, npm's same-version-many-times problem), (b) the lag between a shared library's release and its adoption across consumers, (c) Hyrum's Law on implicit interfaces. Identify metrics that approximate c_drift (interface staleness, version skew, manifest age).

4. Survey the empirical literature on blast-radius reduction from isolation. Cover: (a) Netflix/Hystrix bulkhead pattern and chaos-engineering measurements, (b) Kubernetes namespace isolation impact studies, (c) browser site-isolation (Reis et al), (d) database tenant isolation breach incidents. Identify metrics that approximate c_loss (data exfiltration scope, downtime blast radius, recovery time).

5. Define a measurement plan for the Buuuk/neural-gtm split. Specify, for each of c_modify, c_drift, c_loss, c_storage, c_money, c_find, c_derive: (a) the metric, (b) the source (git history, fs walk, CI logs, manifest age), (c) the pre-split baseline (compute from the pre-2026-05-22 ogilvy state), (d) the post-split measurement (compute now), (e) the expected sign of the delta, (f) the confidence band. The plan should be runnable as a script over /Core/Neural/neural-gtm + /Core/Neural/Buuuk against the pre-split snapshot in /tmp/buuuk_consolidation_backup_2026-05-22/.

6. Estimate, from the literature and the measurement plan, the expected per-axis delta for the Buuuk split. Provide order-of-magnitude estimates with reasoning. Identify which axes the literature predicts will be net-positive (better post-split), net-negative (worse), and uncertain.

7. Derive a decision rule. Under what conditions should A* recommend two-layer separation? Candidates: (a) always for K classes with >1 tenant, (b) only when measured c_drift exceeds threshold T_drift, (c) only when the engine surface stabilizes (test churn below threshold), (d) only above a folder-count threshold (small projects do not benefit). State the rule precisely, including the constants and how they are calibrated.

8. Address the multi-tenant generalization. If Layer A serves N tenants (Buuuk + MAIKAI + TUHH + ...), the costs scale differently. Sketch the per-axis cost as a function of N. Identify the N at which the seam pays for itself, and the N at which the engine bifurcates (because tenants diverge in their constraints).

9. Address the inverse question: when should A* recommend collapsing a two-layer architecture back into one? (The seam is not free; if c_modify has risen and c_drift has not fallen, the split is a mistake.) State the inverse decision rule.

10. Recommend the v0.2 decision: should two-layer separation be a default for K=outbound-pipeline, an optimization triggered by a measured condition, or a tenant-count-dependent rule? Tie the recommendation to the measurement plan: which post-split numbers, if observed on Buuuk/neural-gtm, would confirm the recommendation, and which would falsify it.

Deliverable: a structured research memo with the literature survey, the measurement plan (runnable spec), the per-axis delta estimates, the decision rule (forward and inverse), the multi-tenant scaling sketch, and the v0.2 recommendation with falsifiers. Full citations.
